title: Single-element array of objects - the array-vs-scalar ambiguity
rationale: The classic ambiguity, decided the wrong way by an explicit numeric threshold rather than by accident: analyzeStructure requires parsed.size() > 1 before flagging a prefix as an array. One element never qualifies. Same document as the two-element fixture with one element removed, so the corpus contains the exact pair that isolates the threshold.
catchesBugClass: Cardinality-dependent behaviour: any code path whose correctness depends on how many elements happened to be in the input. This is the shape that makes a pipeline pass in test and corrupt in production on single-row days.
cannotCatch: Which of the two co-occurring failures is primary - the missing array wrapper or the unparsed leaf - because both follow from the same isArray=false decision. It also cannot tell us what the correct answer is for a genuinely one-element array versus a scalar; that needs schema, not inference.

predicted.detail: Both the array wrapper and the value types are lost. Flattens correctly, but both columns parse to size 1, fail the > 1 test, so users becomes an object path and the leaves are never parsed.
